Subject: MAP request: token economics + ops gating before exec review

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency numbers and the fallback policies. We need to put together a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for procurement and engineering to justify the product choice to our execs. Two asks upfront:

1) Can you capture the token/unit economics sensitivity (tokens per USD) for the model you're recommending plus best/worst case when caching and batching are applied?
2) We also need a concise ops gating checklist (what infra/monitoring items must be in place for us to go live in pilot) and an aggressive close timeline (POC -> procurement -> pilot start).

Priya and I will present a one-page summary to the CIO next Friday, so if you can send a MAP draft with numbers and assumptions by EOD Thursday that would help.

Thanks — Liam

--
Liam O'Connor
Director of Product, MedSys Health
liam.oconnor@medsys.com

From: logan_wright@redwood.ai

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP request: token economics + ops gating before exec review

Hi Liam / Priya —

Appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a first-pass MAP focused on the items you flagged. High-level summary up front:

- Recommended model: Open-Variant-X (quantized to 4-bit profile we validated)
- Baseline token throughput (unoptimized): ~3,200 tokens / USD
- Expected tokens/USD after caching & batching: 3,200 -> 4,600 tokens / USD (conservative) up to 6,500 tokens / USD (optimistic)

Key assumptions baked into these numbers (short):
- Average request size: 420 tokens (prompt + expected completion).
- Caching: prefix/KV cache will reduce repeated prompt tokens by ~18% on a typical EHR query workload; if templates-heavy queries apply, expect 25–30% uplift.
- Batching & scheduling: continuous batching with target latency SLO <= 250ms P95 for interactive paths; batching improves per-token efficiency by ~12–18% depending on request arrival rate and timeout window.
- Model quantization & kernel selection: production profile uses 4-bit quantization; measured perf on dedicated pool is ~1.6x cost improvement vs fp16 for inference ops.

Ops gating checklist (short):
- Observability: per-route token-level usage + latency traces in Console (required)
- Alerting: token burn rate spike alert + model quality regression alert tied to eval suite (required)
- Security: SOC2 summary & KMS key integration for logs (provided as attachment)
- Capacity: dedicated pool reservation or burst policy defined for pilot months 1–3 (we recommend a 1.5x headroom commit for burst)
- Rollout policy: canary traffic split + auto-fallback to smaller model variant if SLOs degrade (we'll manage via Redwood Console)

Tactical MAP milestones / timeline (aggressive):
- Thu 19 Feb: Redwood sends this MAP + spreadsheet (attached) — action: MedSys review
- Mon 23 Feb: Technical POC kickoff (3 weeks) — action: sample dataset + eval prompts from MedSys
- Mon 16 Mar: POC review; begin procurement paperwork if metrics meet acceptance
- End Mar: Contract execution & Dedicated capacity reserve
- Apr 5: Pilot start (2-week smoke + ramp)

I've attached medsys_map_token-ops_v1.xlsx with the sensitivity table and conservative/optimistic scenarios. Ben — adding you here for procurement cadence and any discount packaging notes.

If you want, we can convert the first page of the spreadsheet into a one-pager for the CIO.

Cheers,
Logan

--
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.ai
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medsys.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP request: token economics + ops gating before exec review

Thanks Logan — this is exactly the shape we need. Quick clarifying Qs before I hand to the CIO:

1) On the baseline 3,200 tokens/USD number — what model batch size / punctuality assumptions underlie that? Is that steady-state on hosted or dedicated?
2) For the caching uplift (18% conservative) — is that measured on sample queries you ran during the demo, or a heuristic?
3) On the capacity commit: what happens if our production traffic ramps faster than the 1.5x headroom in month 1? How do you handle immediate burst capacity?

Priya — can you attach a short list of 10–12 canonical prompts we will use in the POC? That will help Logan rerun the exact sensitivity numbers for our templates.

Regards,
Liam
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medsys.com>
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP request: token economics + ops gating before exec review

Hi Liam — looping in procurement next steps. Short answers to your questions + next steps: 

1) Baseline 3,200 tokens/USD: measured on dedicated pool with burst disabled, batching window 20ms, average batch size ~6 for 420-token requests. Hosted would be ~10–12% less efficient due to multi-tenant kernel variance; we explicitly used dedicated measurements in the spreadsheet.

2) Caching uplift: we measured the conservative 18% from the demo dataset you shared (some repeated template text). We also modeled a template-heavy scenario at 28% uplift which is in the optimistic column. We'll re-run with Priya's canonical prompts to finalize.

3) Burst capacity: Redwood supports automated short-term burst to shared capacity for immediate needs (up to 2x for a short window) while Dedicated reserve is scaled (billing pro-rated). For production risk: we recommend a staged ramp with an emergency escalation playbook (we'll provide an SLA amendment for burst tiers on signature).

Procurement note: based on the MAP and an initial 6-month pilot, we can offer a 5% commitment credit for the first quarter if MedSys signs a 6-month reserved capacity agreement (deal id DL-8742-MED). I'll put the draft term sheet in the Drive link by EOD Friday.

Attaching SOC2 summary and the MAP spreadsheet; happy to convert the top-line into a one-pager for your CIO.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
